name: Mawlynnong
tagline: Asia's cleanest village tucked in Meghalaya's living-root heartland
highlights: asia's cleanest village with bamboo dustbins and immaculate lanes
living root bridges and crystal-clear dawki river nearby

attractions.name: Mawlynnong Village
attractions.description: Awarded Asia's Cleanest Village by Discover India magazine, Mawlynnong is a spotless Khasi hamlet of 500 people who have collectively maintained pristine stone-paved lanes, flower-draped houses, and bamboo dustbin towers for generations. The entire village operates as a community-led eco-tourism model, with home-stays, guided walks, and a 100% literacy rate that is as impressive as its cleanliness.
attractions.whyVisit: Experience a genuinely unique community that has turned cleanliness and sustainability into a living culture.
attractions.mapsSearch: Mawlynnong Village, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya

attractions.name: Mawlynnong Living Root Bridge
attractions.description: A single-span living root bridge crafted over two centuries by training the aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees across a stream, this bridge near Mawlynnong village is one of Meghalaya's most photographed natural wonders. Moss-covered, springy underfoot, and embedded in lush jungle, it represents the Khasi tribe's ingenious bio-engineering that produces bridges stronger than any wooden structure.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the most accessible and beautiful living root bridges in Meghalaya.
attractions.bestTime: October to May; early morning for fewer crowds

attractions.name: Dawki River and Umngot River
attractions.description: The Umngot River at Dawki, 30 km from Mawlynnong, is often called the cleanest river in India — the water is so crystal clear that boats appear to float on glass, their reflections and the river bed visible simultaneously. Coracle boating here during winter is a surreal, otherworldly experience against a backdrop of limestone cliffs and the Bangladesh border hills.
attractions.whyVisit: The glass-clear boating experience is one of the most visually arresting sights in all of Northeast India.
attractions.bestTime: November to April for clearest water
attractions.imageQuery: Dawki Umngot River clear water boat Meghalaya

attractions.name: Sky Walk (Bamboo Viewpoint), Mawlynnong
attractions.description: A tall bamboo treehouse-style tower at the edge of Mawlynnong village offers an elevated view over the dense forest canopy and, on clear days, the plains of Bangladesh stretching to the horizon. The structure itself — entirely built from bamboo without a single nail — is a feat of traditional Khasi construction that doubles as an exhibit of vernacular architecture.
attractions.whyVisit: Unique vantage point with views into Bangladesh and above the jungle canopy.
attractions.mapsSearch: Mawlynnong Sky Walk Bamboo Viewpoint, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Mawlynnong bamboo sky walk viewpoint Meghalaya

attractions.name: Riwai Living Root Bridge
attractions.description: Just 1 km from Mawlynnong village, the Riwai single-decker root bridge is often less crowded than the main village bridge and is set in a particularly lush jungle gully. The short forest trail to reach it passes through banana plantations and betel-nut groves and is one of the most pleasant short walks in the region.
attractions.whyVisit: A quieter, equally beautiful root bridge with a more adventurous approach trail.

attractions.name: Nohwet Village
attractions.description: A small Khasi hamlet a short drive from Mawlynnong, Nohwet is known for its traditional matrilineal family structures, betel-nut cultivation, and community weaving. Unlike Mawlynnong, which receives tourist traffic, Nohwet offers an unfiltered look at everyday rural Khasi life, with older women in traditional jainsem attire going about their daily routines.
attractions.whyVisit: Authentic village experience away from tourist traffic, deep in Khasi culture.
attractions.mapsSearch: Nohwet Village, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya

attractions.name: Pynursla
attractions.description: The small town of Pynursla serves as the nearest commercial hub for Mawlynnong and marks the beginning of the narrow road that descends to the Bangladesh border plain. The surrounding area is rich in betel-nut plantations and gives a good sense of the landscape transition from the Khasi plateau to the Bengal lowlands.
attractions.whyVisit: Last town before the remote Mawlynnong cluster; good for supplies and local food.

attractions.name: Bholaganj Border Area
attractions.description: Located near the Bangladesh border, the Bholaganj area features a dramatic boulder-strewn riverbed where white stones cascade down from the hills — a natural spectacle created by millenia of river erosion. The site is close to Mawlynnong and is a popular day excursion for visitors to the region, with the international border visible from the river banks.
attractions.whyVisit: A striking natural landscape with river boulders and views to Bangladesh.

attractions.name: Dawki Suspension Bridge
attractions.description: The old colonial-era suspension bridge spanning the Umngot River at Dawki is a British-built iron structure that still carries traffic between India and the Bangladesh border checkpoint. Walking across it offers dramatic views of the impossibly clear river below and the green hills framing the border valley.
attractions.whyVisit: A historic bridge with spectacular views over the clearest river in India.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning to avoid border traffic
attractions.mapsSearch: Dawki Suspension Bridge, Umngot River, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Dawki suspension bridge Meghalaya clear river

attractions.name: Shnongpdeng
attractions.description: A short drive upriver from Dawki, Shnongpdeng has become a hub for adventure activities on the Umngot River — snorkelling in the crystal-clear water to see fish swimming over a sandy riverbed, cliff jumping, kayaking, and camping on the riverbanks. The water visibility here is often more than 10 metres, making it a remarkable freshwater snorkelling site.
attractions.whyVisit: The only place in India where you can snorkel in crystal-clear freshwater and see the riverbed perfectly.

attractions.name: Nartiang Durga Temple
attractions.description: An important Shakta pilgrimage site located in Nartiang town, the Durga temple complex here is one of Meghalaya's most significant Hindu shrines. Adjacent to the temple stands the Nartiang Monolith Park — a collection of the largest grouping of monoliths in Asia, erected by the Jaintia kings as memorials, some reaching 8 metres in height.
attractions.whyVisit: Combines an active Hindu temple with Asia's largest monolith field in a single remarkable stop.
attractions.mapsSearch: Nartiang Durga Temple and Monolith Park, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Nartiang monolith park Meghalaya stone pillars

attractions.name: Wahkhen Village
attractions.description: A remote Khasi village near the Bangladesh border escarpment, Wahkhen offers sweeping views of the plains below from its clifftop setting. The village is known among birdwatchers for its raptor migration corridor — thousands of raptors, including Amur falcons and Oriental honey buzzards, pass through between October and November.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the best raptor migration watch-points in Northeast India during autumn.
attractions.bestTime: October to November for migration; year-round for views
attractions.mapsSearch: Wahkhen Village, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Wahkhen cliff viewpoint raptor migration Meghalaya

attractions.name: Mawkyrwat
attractions.description: A small scenic town in South West Khasi Hills, Mawkyrwat is the gateway to several remote waterfalls and living root bridges less visited than those near Mawlynnong. The surrounding forest retains a wild character and the town itself hosts a lively weekly market where tribal communities from surrounding villages trade produce and crafts.
attractions.whyVisit: Gateway to remote waterfalls and root bridges without the tourist footfall.
attractions.mapsSearch: Mawkyrwat, South West Khasi Hills, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Mawkyrwat forest waterfall South Khasi Hills

attractions.name: Lyngkhat Village
attractions.description: A quiet Khasi settlement between Pynursla and Mawlynnong, Lyngkhat is surrounded by betel-nut and areca-palm groves and is known for its traditional community-managed sacred forests. These 'Law Kyntang' groves are protected by centuries of Khasi custom and harbour mature trees and wildlife rarely found outside forest reserves.
attractions.whyVisit: Witness a community-protected sacred forest — a living example of indigenous conservation.
attractions.mapsSearch: Lyngkhat Village, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya
attractions.imageQuery: Lyngkhat sacred forest Khasi village Meghalaya

attractions.name: Borderland Resort Area, Dawki
attractions.description: The stretch of river immediately below the Dawki bridge is where most boating operators launch their transparent-bottomed and regular coracles onto the Umngot. The setting — hemmed by forest-covered limestone hills on one side and the Bangladesh border post on the other — gives a peculiar edge-of-the-world feeling utterly unique in India.
attractions.whyVisit: The iconic boat-on-glass photo opportunity and border landscape of Dawki.
attractions.bestTime: November to March for best water clarity
attractions.mapsSearch: Dawki Boat Point, Meghalaya India Bangladesh border
attractions.imageQuery: Dawki boat glass water border Meghalaya

attractions.name: Mawjymbuin Cave, near Mawsynram
attractions.description: Located near Mawsynram — the wettest place on Earth — the Mawjymbuin cave contains a massive naturally formed stalagmite shaped like a Shiva lingam that is revered by local Hindus. The cave opens into a high chamber with dramatic formations and underground streams, offering a powerful combination of geological and spiritual wonder.
attractions.whyVisit: A spectacular cave with a revered natural rock formation near the world's wettest place.

attractions.name: Jakrem Hot Springs
attractions.description: Situated 64 km from Shillong and used as a day trip from Mawlynnong, the Jakrem hot springs are sulphurous thermal springs that locals and visitors use for bathing, believed to cure skin ailments. The setting in a forested valley with a cool Meghalayan climate makes the warm spring water especially pleasant from October onwards.
attractions.whyVisit: A naturally therapeutic hot-spring soak in a beautiful forested Meghalaya valley.
attractions.imageQuery: Jakrem hot springs thermal bath Meghalaya
